You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

task-c9860f8b SOLVED (3 demos used, 1 wrong attempt). RULE: gap filling between collinear marks. Identify mark color (sparse color) vs background. Mark cells KEEP their color. A background cell becomes color 3 iff there is at least one mark on BOTH sides in the same row OR the same column (nearest mark each direction, any distance, marks block). All other background cells KEEP the original background color. Only horizontal/vertical lines fill - collinear DIAGONAL marks do NOT fill gaps (verified demo3). Worked examples: demo1 (23x25, sparse 5s in 6s -> most 6s filled since ~6 marks/row), demo3 (16x26, sparse 7s -> almost nothing filled). Test 5x25: only (1,13) filled between marks (1,12),(1,14). Lessons: (a) when kept/removed looks 5x5-neighborhood-determined but unexplainable by counts/components/distance, check GEOMETRIC line-of-sight rules (cell between two same-colored marks in row/col); (b) verify the hypothesis on ALL demos programmatically before submitting; (c) never hand-transcribe long demo grid rows - I introduced OCR errors retyping demo3, parse programmatically.

arc_task_c9860f8b_rule_gap_filling_between_collinear_marks_fill_color_3
task-c9860f8b SOLVED again (1 demo, 0 wrong). RULE: gap filling between collinear marks. Mark color = sparse color (0 in demo, 2 in test), background = dominant color, fill color = 3. A background cell becomes 3 iff a mark exists strictly ABOVE and strictly BELOW in its column, OR strictly LEFT and strictly RIGHT in its row (marks anywhere along the line, unblocked scan — equivalent to filling segments between consecutive collinear marks since splitting at an intermediate mark yields the same union). Marks and other background cells keep their color. Implementation: out[r][c]=3 for background cells with (any mark above and below in column) or (any mark left and right in row). Verified exactly on demo; test (mark=2, 26x22) filled 326/471 background cells; submission CORRECT.

task-c9860f8b SOLVED (2 wrong attempts, 3 demos). CONFIRMED RULE: background and mark cells keep their colors; every background cell strictly between two CONSECUTIVE mark cells in its row or column (all cells between are background) becomes 3. NO distance cap (gap of 10 filled in demo3). Fill color is always 3 regardless of bg/mark colors (demos: bg1/m2->3, bg4/m8->none, bg9/m7->3). Marks are the sparse non-background color; detect bg = most common color. Isolated marks with no aligned partner stay unchanged; dominoes (adjacent marks) produce no fill. KEY LESSONS: (1) attempt1 was a false refutation - the submitted grid contained 34 diagonal-artifact 3s from a buggy helper, while the intended rule was correct; ALWAYS diff the submitted output against a clean, independent reimplementation before submitting. (2) A wrong attempt does not necessarily refute the rule family - first re-verify your own output generation. (3) A single no-op demo (no aligned marks) is uninformative about distance limits; request another demo before assuming a cap. (4) Verify demos against candidate rules programmatically (np.array_equal), and use diff lists (mismatched cells) to debug.

arc_task_c9860f8b_rule_clear_cross_visibility_fill_with_color_3
ARC task-c9860f8b SOLVED (2 demos, 0 wrong). FAMILY 'visibility shadow fill': input has two colors: background (dominant, e.g. 0, 5, or 7) and scattered shape cells (5, 0, or 8). RULE: every background cell is checked with a 'clear cross': it stays background iff there is a clear straight line (no shape cells) from it to the top OR bottom edge AND to the left OR right edge. Otherwise (blocked vertically on both sides OR horizontally on both sides) it becomes fill color 3. Shape cells stay unchanged (one rare 5->3 anomaly in demo1 cell (7,6), likely noise). Fill color is ALWAYS 3 regardless of palette (verified with two different palettes: 0/5->3 and 5/0->3, and test 7/8->3). Equivalent formulation: hidden = (shape above AND shape below in column) OR (shape left AND shape right in row); those cells -> 3. Verified: demo1 0 bg-mismatches, demo2 3 mismatches in one row only (demo text was garbled; likely transcription noise). Python helper: for bg cell (r,c): vok = all bg above OR all bg below; hok = all bg left OR all bg right; keep bg if vok and hok else 3. Note: flood-fill from border does NOT work (fails ~50% cells).

arc_task_c9860f8b_rule_fill_row_span_between_outermost_marker_cells_with_3
task-c9860f8b SOLVED (2 demos, 1 wrong attempt). FAMILY 'marker span fill': grid = mostly one background color (e.g. all-2, all-9, all-7) scattered with marker cells of one other color (4 or 5). RULE: for each ROW, find the leftmost and rightmost marker cell; fill all cells strictly between them with 3. Cells outside the span, single-marker rows, and the markers themselves stay unchanged. Output dims = input dims. PITFALL: it is NOT 'all background -> 3' (that failed once); edges beyond the outermost marker in each row keep the background color. Demo1: 4s at cols 2,3,4,9 in one row -> cols 5-8 became 3; a lone 4 in another row stayed; a lone 4 anywhere -> row unchanged. Works the same when markers are 5s on 9-background.

Output: fill with color 3 every background cell that has at least one dot on each side along its row AND along its column (fill between consecutive dots horizontally and vertically; no diagonals). Verified on demo3 (5x16, horizontal) and demo1 (23x24, matched 483/485 cells; 2 mismatches were transcription typos). Degenerate inputs with no dots map to themselves unchanged.

arc_dot_fill_family_tactic_task_c9860f8b_and_similar
FAMILY 'dot fill between consecutive dots' — verified on task-c9860f8b (solved, 0 wrong, 3 demos).

SIGNAL: grid is uniform background color with scattered single 'dot' cells of another color (seen: 4 on 1, 0 on 8, 6 on 2). Dot counts ~5-70.

RULE: for each background cell, check its row and its column separately. If the cell has at least one dot somewhere to its left AND one to its right (same row), OR one above AND one below (same column), set it to 3. Dots and all other cells stay. NO diagonal fills (tested: adding diagonals caused 50 mismatches on demo1; HV-only gave 2 mismatches = transcription typos).

OUTPUT FILL COLOR: 3 in all observed instances regardless of input colors.

DEGENERATE CASE: input with zero dots maps to itself unchanged (demo2 was an all-background 12x5 grid -> identical output).

METHOD LESSON: demos for this task can be degenerate (empty grid) — one blank demo still gives info (confirms dot-dependence). When first demo is a large confusing pattern, verify candidate rules programmatically against the demo (flood fills, visible-pair segments, ray parity, MST/RNG all FAILED; simple 'dot on each side along row/col' was correct). Beware hand-transcription typos when copying grids: a couple of mismatched cells may be your own copy errors, not rule errors.

global_task_c9860f8b_rule_fill_between_aligned_markers_final
task-c9860f8b SOLVED (this instance: 1 wrong attempt, 4 demo requests). RECURRING task family 'gap fill between aligned markers' (earlier memories arc_task_c9860f8b_* describe the same rule).

FINAL CONFIRMED RULE (exact fit on 4 demo pairs incl. 7x9 demo4):
- Background = dominant color; markers = the other color(s).
- A bg cell becomes 3 iff it lies strictly between two markers that share its row OR its column (any pair, even spanning other markers; union over all pairs = full span between extreme markers in that row/col).
- ALL marker cells keep their color (3 never replaces a marker, even markers strictly between other markers or in adjacent marker pairs).
- No diagonal fills (refuted: demos have many unfilled diag-between cells). No edge effects; segment length unlimited (gap 8 filled in demo3 col0).

CRITICAL BUG THAT CAUSED THE WRONG ATTEMPT: an ad-hoc fill loop wrote 3 into cells without checking the cell is background, silently converting marker cells to 3. ALWAYS generate the submission via the verified solve() on the test input and verify marker cells are unchanged. Also: a transcription error in a stored demo output (O3 rows10-11 col0) cost debugging time - when a verified rule 'almost' fits (1-3 cells off), suspect transcription errors in the stored expected output before abandoning the rule.

solve() code: bg = Counter of grid flattened .most_common(1); o=deep copy; for each row and each column: ms=sorted(marker positions); for every pair (i<j) set o=3 for indices strictly between ms[i],ms[j] ONLY IF cell is bg.
